answer: Latency anchor pools. Each identity must anchor to a rotating pool of independent relays and maintain a stable round-trip baseline; a deliberate delay is injected before any action is accepted, and the delay schedule wanders across pools on a slow random walk. Sybil fleets cannot predict the schedule, and an attacker who lets timing drift to probe it loses the anchor. A reef of decoy pools traps newly forked identities, forcing them to spend real setup latency per puppet.
